name: MEV bot 0x05f0 unprotected swap entry point
summary: The MEV bot contract exposed selector 0xf6ebebbb, an internal swap-execution entry point, with no caller check and no output validation. A flash-loan-funded attacker called it directly with pool and amount parameters of their own choosing and moved the contract’s whole USDC, USDT, WETH and WBTC balance out through the pools it was told to trade against.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract. The runtime code hash is 0x3fcd64f33e1dad69ad1681df62dfac7f3cc7c82e817f71899ffa07937571f687 both at the deployment block 18370467 and at block 18523343, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

Components are the victim contract’s net ERC-20 balance deltas in the single exploit transaction, which is the first transaction of block 18523344. The attacker’s later transaction to the same exploit contract at block 18537100 does not touch the victim. BlockSec’s contemporaneous alert put the loss near USD 2 million; this exact netting at DefiLlama prices for the incident timestamp is higher. Nothing was recovered.
